findings.text: Node statistics query exposes per-node counter values for a given item, with a pages-oriented helper that reads the underlying atomic store. Callers supply the node descriptor and item selector and receive an unsigned count.

Slab cache accounting helper fills a caller-provided summary from per-node slab and object totals plus an approximation of free objects in partial slabs, also reporting per-slab density and order derived from cache geometry.
Swap cache diagnostic has two shapes: an empty inline form and a reporting form that announces cached page count together with free and total swap capacities in kilobytes.
Unreclaimable slab diagnostic has an empty inline form and a reporting form that attempts non-blocking protection of the cache list and, when successful, reports usage for caches holding objects.
Sharing test determines whether any thread of a process is associated with a given address space, using the first thread that currently holds such an association as representative.
Memory cgroup OOM helpers resolve the relevant ancestor group for a victim within an OOM domain and emit group-oriented diagnostics that include cgroup path information.

Charging context resolver maps an address space, active scope, or current task to the accountable memory cgroup, with special handling for disabled accounting and for contexts lacking an address space.
System-wide drain entry scans online processors and arranges flushing of cached page and object charges that belong under a given root.
High-limit enforcement entry reclaims overage for the current allocator hierarchy and applies throttling when reclaim does not bring usage below configured thresholds.

Memory availability summary diagnostic reports per-order free extents with migration hints and totals, plus per-node large-page details where not filtered out, followed by page-cache and swap-cache totals.

Victim termination pipeline handles already-exiting victims via reserve access and deferred reclamation, otherwise announces context under rate control, delivers fatal signals to the victim and to unrelated sharers of its address space, and schedules deferred reclamation when permitted.
Panic policy gate decides whether an OOM context escalates to a system halt based on administrative setting, constraint scope, and trigger origin, emitting a header before halting.
Presence encoding uses letter U for unmovable, M for movable, E for reclaimable, H for high atomic, with C for contiguous when that option is enabled and I for isolated when that option is enabled.
Node counter reads treat negative stored values as zero on multiprocessor builds and flag misuse when the requested item is measured in bytes rather than pages.
Unreclaimable slab reporting skips caches marked as reclaim-accounted and omits caches without objects, expressing used and total capacities from object counts scaled by object size.
Summary active counts equal total objects minus approximated free objects, while slab counts reflect summed per-node slab totals.

A task is considered soon to release memory only when it has an address space, is not marked to skip reclamation, is not engaged in core dumping, shows group exit or single-thread exit progress, and has no unrelated sharer of the same address space that fails the same test.

Group OOM resolution applies only on the default hierarchy, defaults an absent domain to the root, ignores victims in the root or outside the domain, and selects the highest ancestor carrying the group marker, holding a reference on success.

Per-processor charge-cache consumption requires the request to fit within the batch bound, a matching cached group entry, and sufficient cached pages; emptying an entry releases its reference and clears the slot.
A processor cache needs flushing when it holds a cached entry whose accountable group descends from the drain root, with page caches additionally requiring a non-zero page count.

Node filtering is inactive without the node-filter flag; otherwise a node is skipped when absent from the supplied mask or, when no mask is given, from the current allowed set. Managed-zone presence is true when any zone up to the bound reports managed pages.
Node annotation emits the owning node identifier only when non-uniform memory support is enabled.

Free-area snapshot protection releases the zone lock with interrupt state restoration before emitting order lines. Slab diagnostic list traversal uses a non-blocking mutex attempt rather than sleeping. Global drain coordination uses a non-blocking mutex attempt to avoid duplicate workers.

Process and memory-hierarchy traversals run under read-side RCU protection, including sharing checks, OOM group walks, cgroup path reporting, and cached-entry scans. Per-processor stock updates use local locking with a non-blocking attempt for fast-path consumption and a held lock for draining.

Victim assessment holds the task lock while testing future release and marking reserve access. Address-space sharing termination acquires the victim address-space association under lock and retains a grab across unlock for later comparison. Drain-all disables migration across the online-processor scan.
Slab summary layout carries active and total object counts, active and total slab counts, objects per slab, and cache order.

Per-processor page-charge cache holds an array of cached group references with corresponding page counts plus flags and deferred work; object-charge cache holds an array of cached object-group references plus flags and deferred work.

OOM handling observes victim identity and grouping fields including chosen task, target domain, constraint kind, node mask, signal grouping state, exit flags, address-space user count and reclamation markers, and per-task reaper timer state.

Victim lifecycle moves among selection, early release path with deferred reclamation, fatal signaling with reserve access, peer sharer signaling, and optional deferred reclamation, with global init pinning forcing a skip marker and suppressing reclamation.

Over-high handling cycles through dying-task abandonment, ancestor reclaim while over threshold, delay computation for memory and swap overages with clamping and insignificance cutoff, progress-based retry, and throttling sleep that can be ended by fatal signals under stall accounting.

Drain coordination moves per-processor caches from idle to flushing via atomic flag acquisition, executes inline for the local processor and via queued work elsewhere unless the target is isolated, then returns to idle after full slot draining and flag clearing.

Slab diagnostics in pressured paths risk sleeping or crashing without protection; the design accepts missing output when non-blocking protection fails rather than blocking. Draining outside task context is treated as a programming error.

Reaper scheduling relies on an atomic queued marker to prevent duplicate timers. Fatal signaling precedes reserve access to avoid reserve depletion. Concurrent group moves that place the victim outside the OOM domain cause group-wide action to be ignored.

Core-dumping tasks are excluded from prompt-release promises due to extended sleep. Single-user address spaces satisfy the promise while shared ones require every unrelated sharer to satisfy it. Skipped address spaces are treated as unlikely to release further memory.
